To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fractal basin boundaries of a large class of discrete dynamical systems modelling a chaotic forcing of bistable systems are identical to the graph functions of infinite weighted series of iterates of chaotic unimodal interval functions.

The fractal basin boundary in a two-dimensional map is identical to the graph F(x,t) of a weighted series of iterates of the logistic function, and is therefore nowhere differentiable, for each t > e-λf."

(i) the fractal basin boundary is identical to the graph F of a weighted series of iterates of a chaotic function, (ii) the series converges for all t>exp(-λf), (iii) F is nowhere-differentiable, (iv) F is a continuous and monotone function, (v) the basin boundary is a graph, (vi) the basin boundary can be computed by a simple numerical algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What is the basin boundary of a chaotic dynamical system, and how can it be computed?
the following question. Is the fractal basin boundary a differentiable function?
the following question: How do the fractal boundaries of basins of attraction look for a discrete dynamical system in the plane?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the basin boundary is nowhere differentiable.
, for a large class of chaotic functions, the basin boundary of the discrete system is identical to the graph (in x,t-plane) of a nowhere differentiable series.
the fractal basin boundary is always a graph of a nowhere-differentiable function, even if it is not a Weierstrass-like function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a simple way to generate fractal basin boundaries of chaotic dynamical systems.

nowhere-differentiability of the basin boundary of a discrete dynamical system is a consequence of the ergodicity of a chaotic function f and of the existence of an invariant measure with a positive Lyapunov exponents for the corresponding dynamical system.
the fractal basin boundary is a nowhere differentiability preserving operator.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the boundary of a chaotic basin of attraction of a dynamical system is not a smooth curve, even if the dynamics is smooth and the initial conditions are smooth, as long as the basin is not simply connected and the dynamics is chaotic.
a chaotic dynamical system with a nowhere-differentiable basin boundary is equivalent to a dynamical system with an ergodic unidirectional chaotic function, which is a very simple dynamical system.
nowhere-differentiability of the basin boundary is a generic property in a wide class of dynamical systems.
